title: Hierarchical Interpretable Multitask Audio Representation Learning: An Analysis of Event-Scene Relationships through the Information Bottleneck
abstract: arXiv:2610.21520v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Joint Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC) and Audio Tagging (AT) models traditionally rely on unconstrained multihead architectures. However, this design ignores the natural hierarchical dependency between sounds and acoustic scenes. In this work, we investigate a hierarchical (sequential) conditioning paradigm that predicts scene categories directly from intermediate event probabilities. Through a large-scale empirical benchmark with 66 full training runs across three state-of-the-art backbones (PaSST, PANNs, and BEATs) and different loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.0, 1.0]), we show that hierarchical conditioning achieves competitive classification performance while altering multitask optimization dynamics. Unlike multihead baselines, which sequentially solve the easier ASC task before optimizing AT, the hierarchical architecture enables synchronized dual-task learning for specific loss-weighting settings (beta in [0.6, 0.9]). translated_title: 层次化可解释的多任务音频表示学习：基于信息瓶颈的事件-场景关系分析
translated_abstract: 传统的联合声学场景分类（ASC）与音频标注（AT）模型通常依赖于无约束的多头架构，然而这种设计忽略了声音与声学场景之间自然的层次依赖关系。在本工作中，我们研究了一种层次化（顺序）条件化范式，即直接从中间事件概率来预测场景类别。通过一项大规模实证基准测试——在三种最先进的骨干网络（PaSST、PANNs和BEATs）上进行66次完整训练，并采用不同的损失权重设置（beta在[0.0, 1.0]范围内）——我们证明层次化条件化方法在改变多任务优化动态的同时，仍能取得具有竞争力的分类性能。与多头基线先解决较简单的ASC任务、再优化AT任务的顺序模式不同，层次化架构在特定损失权重设置（beta在[0.6, 0.9]范围内）下能够实现双任务同步学习。
tldr: 本文提出一种层次化可解释的多任务音频学习范式，直接由音频事件概率预测声学场景，并通过信息瓶颈分析与大规模基准实验证明，该方法在保持分类性能竞争力的同时改变了多任务优化动态，能够在特定损失权重设置下实现事件识别与场景分类的同步学习。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a hierarchical interpretable multitask audio learning paradigm that predicts acoustic scenes directly from intermediate event probabilities, demonstrating through information bottleneck analysis and large-scale benchmarks that it achieves competitive classification performance while altering multitask optimization dynamics to enable synchronized dual-task learning under specific loss-weighting settings.
